idiom_name: presentation struct + html/template (or text/template) Execute into an io.Writer
implementation_notes: The classic structure collapses into two stdlib calls: stage one is a plain struct (or a tree of structs) holding the logical page, and stage two is Template.Execute(w, page) on a template parsed once at start-up. Because Execute takes any io.Writer the same logical page feeds every channel, and the choice of package is the channel decision: html/template escapes by output context for HTML, text/template writes unescaped text for e-mail, CSV and plain-text channels. Templates are safe for concurrent use once parsed, so hold them in package-level variables and use template.Must at init so a broken renderer fails the process instead of a request. Reach for the classic XSLT form only if a declarative stylesheet language is a hard requirement.
pitfalls: html/template escapes by context, so rendering a plain-text or CSV channel through it emits HTML entities - use text/template for non-HTML channels.
Execute writes as it walks the template, so a mid-render error leaves a half-written response; buffer into a bytes.Buffer when the channel cannot be retracted.
A template parsed from user-controlled or per-tenant files is a code-execution surface; keep renderers embedded or loaded from a trusted location, and never from a request path.
